title: ApplyOps
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> apply <ops.json>` (CLI-SPEC §7) — an ORDERED array of op-records applied to ONE model in a single session: one read → ordered surgery → one terminal kernel gate → one write, with atomic rollback (a mid-sequence failure writes nothing). Each op-record is {target, op, …args}; the per-op fields are that verb's params — discover them from `manifest` + `schema <target> <op>`. The op-set spans add·modify·remove·read PLUS the reference-rewriting refactors: `field`/`group` rename·move, `rule` rename, `typedef` rename (each runs its §6 safety gate at its turn against the live model — a refused refactor rolls the whole sequence back). A `group remove` takes the same `cascade` safe-delete gate as the standalone verb (a group still referenced from outside its subtree is refused unless `cascade:true`); `rule remove` deletes a rule. `extract`/`inline` stay standalone verbs. An unsupported target/op self-corrects via RK_UNKNOWN_OP, which lists the ops apply DOES support. Distinct from `batch` (which takes {verb, args} for stateless per-op dispatch). Each op emits a per-op result envelope (a successful edit is `staged` until the terminal gate commits the whole sequence); the wrapper is {ops, committed, failedAt, written, results[]}.

target.description: the element family acted on: field | group | rule | … (see `manifest`)

op.description: the operation: add | modify | remove | read | rename | move (valid for the target; see `manifest`)
